transcript.text: vax upright brush thingy stopped spinnin, sucks ok thru the hose but nt pickin up off carpet. smelt like burnin rubber b4 it stopped

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Because you smelled burning rubber before the brush stopped, this appliance must not be used again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The burning smell indicates that something was overheating—likely the drive belt slipping on a jammed roller or an electrical fault in the brush motor—and continuing to use it could cause a fire or damage the main suction motor. I can explain what likely happened so you know what to expect when you get it repaired. In Vax uprights, this sequence usually means one of two things:
1. The rubber drive belt snapped (often because hair and thread had jammed the brush bar, causing the motor to strain until the belt gave way). This is common and cheap to fix.
2. The separate electric motor that spins the brush bar failed or its thermal cut-out tripped permanently due to overheating. Since I cannot safely inspect the internal components while it is powered on, and because a burnt smell suggests potential damage to wiring or insulation, please arrange for a professional repair. Do not attempt to open the casing or test electrical parts yourself.

candidates: Drive belt snapped due to overload or age (high)
Brush bar motor failed (thermal cut-out triggered) (medium)

reading.symptom: brush stopped spinning, not picking up from carpet

plan: Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Vax.
The fault they reported is: "brush stopped spinning, not picking up from carpet". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
